findings.problem: Output schema of demo.message.propose allows only status pending_approval|approved. An idempotent repeat (same key and args) of an intent that has moved on returns 200 with status succeeded/executing/failed/...; the MCP client validates structuredContent against the published outputSchema and raises RuntimeError instead of returning the existing intent. No test repeats propose after a status change
findings.reproduction: demo fixtures, MockApi answering 200 {intent_id, status: 'succeeded'} -> ClientSession.call_tool raises 'Invalid structured content returned by tool demo.message.propose: ... is not one of [pending_approval, approved]'
findings.required_improvement: status enum = the 11 statuses of schemas/intent-status.schema.json; end-to-end test on the real stack: propose -> succeeded -> same propose again -> 200, same intent_id, status succeeded through a real MCP client

findings.problem: With no signing key whose not_before has passed, the executor still reserves; SigningKeys.current() raises, the attempt becomes T12a and counts; the intent is re-queued at once and ends failed after max_attempts within a second. This is the state right after the documented compromise step with one key (keys rotate + keys remove --compromised) and after removing the old key before the new key's not_before. README says the opposite («исполнения ждут rotate + 15 мин»); human approvals are lost and the recorded error 'no_response' hides the cause
findings.reproduction: test_executor.py stack, signing = [{seed, not_before: 2999-01-01}], 10 x run_once -> status failed, executions [(1|2|3, failed_before_effect, no_response)], attempts 3
findings.required_improvement: in take(): no active key -> do not reserve, keep the outbox row undelivered (as the kill-switch deferral), no attempt counted; test: no active key -> intent approved, attempts 0, no executions; key active -> executed. Fix the README row

findings.ref: AS-10, SEC-10 (rotation documented and at least every 90 days), AC-M8-14, AS-28
findings.problem: In the reference compose the executor's key file is a Docker secret (single-file bind mount); keys rotate/remove write with os.replace, and a single-file bind mount keeps the old inode, so the executor never sees the new key without a restart (and after the old key leaves the JWKS every dispatch is refused). The CLI needs both files in one place, but the JWKS lives in api's ./config and the key file only in the executor secret; --compromised needs the executor DB DSN and the internal network that the host cannot reach. cli._keys and cli._executor have no test; cli._keys duplicates the release SQL of Executor.release_reserved. AC-M8-14 passes only in one process with in-memory lists
findings.reproduction: docker run -v $D/keys:/run/secrets/keys:ro postgres:16.6-alpine; python os.replace($D/keys.tmp, $D/keys) on the host -> host 'v2', docker exec cat /run/secrets/keys -> 'v1'
findings.required_improvement: mount the executor key file from a directory (as api's ./config) and assert it in test_deploy.py; README: which command runs where (rotate/remove on the host over the two directories, the AS-10 release inside the executor container); a test of cli.main(['keys','remove','--kid',K,'--compromised']) against the DB, with the CLI calling one release function

findings.problem: The temp file with the new private seed is created with the default umask (usually 0644) and chmod 0600 only afterwards: a window where any local user who can list the directory reads the seed
findings.required_improvement: create the temp file with os.open(..., O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC, mode)

findings.problem: httpx.Client per service id cached for the process lifetime; a bundle that changes the connector's internal_url is ignored, refused connections become T12a and intents fail after 3 attempts

Removing CONTINUE WHEN (x.e).state <> 'reserved' is labelled equivalent but is not: an execution dispatched between the loop's SELECT and the lock is set to released, then _gxg_check refuses reserve_lease_expired from dispatching (GX409) and the whole call aborts, releasing nothing. No double effect (safety holds), but the guard is untested; a deterministic test with a held intent row lock is possible
findings.required_improvement: test: lock the intent, move its execution to dispatching, run gxg_release_reserved in a thread, commit -> the dispatching execution stays, the other reserved ones are released; drop the 'equivalent:' prefix of that row

findings.problem: The hash is checked on canonical.normalize(args), but the provider gets the raw body args: an NFD text passes the check and is sent as NFD (different text_hash than approved). Only a broken or compromised executor sends that: defence in depth
findings.required_improvement: send the normalized args kept from the check
